title: From Differential Equations to Discrete Problems

contract.reader: An engineer or student who knows calculus, basic linear algebra and ODEs and is about to use or write a PDE solver without knowing what discretization does to the answer
contract.problem: How a PDE becomes a finite algebraic problem, and what error, order, consistency, stability and convergence mean for the result
contract.outcome: Classify a model PDE and state the conditions it needs; derive a difference quotient and its truncation error; solve the 1D Poisson problem; measure an observed order; recognize a boundary treatment that spoils the order
contract.contribution: One path from physical model to verified discrete solution, with every order claim checked by a runnable script and every predicted error constant compared with the measured one
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; three scripts with real output; Higham, IEEE 754-2019, LeVeque, Morton and Mayers, Strauss, Strikwerda
contract.limitations: Finite differences on uniform 1D grids only; finite volumes not covered; time stepping and the Lax equivalence theorem deferred to entry 2

findings.location: Section 5.1, the forward/central difference display (1280 px, desktop-light-11); all three Section 5.1 formulas at 360 px (mobile-light-20/21)
findings.problem: At 1280 px the central-difference formula is cut after 'u(x-'; its right-hand side with the h^2/6 truncation term is hidden behind an unmarked sideways scroll. At 360 px the Taylor expansion, forward and second differences also lose their truncation terms
findings.whyItMatters: The truncation terms are the result of the section; Section 5.2 checks h^2/6 and Section 6.1 uses h^2/12
findings.action: Put the forward and central differences in separate displays (or an aligned block) and break the Taylor expansion and second difference over lines
findings.acceptance: Both difference formulas fully visible at 1280 px; at 360 px every Section 5.1 formula shows its truncation term without scrolling

findings.problem: Five displays are wider than the phone column; the hidden parts include Delta x = L/N, the index range and the boundary conditions of the 6.1 and 6.2 problems
findings.whyItMatters: Phone readers see problems stated without the conditions the subsection is about
findings.action: Split each display so equation and conditions are on separate lines
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the five displays are fully visible, or the hidden part is not needed to read the equation

findings.location: Section 1.1, Mermaid modeling chain (360 px, mobile-light-04)
findings.problem: Only the first two stages are visible; Discrete problem and Computed numbers are off-screen with no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: The diagram introduces the error sources the page is organized around
findings.action: flowchart TB layout, or the site-level scroll cue for wide figures
findings.acceptance: At 360 px all four stages are visible or a visible cue shows the figure scrolls
